Music beneath Wawel’s illuminated arcades KRAKÓW — The 19th edition of the Wawel at Dusk summer music festival reaches its finale on Sunday, 9 August, bringing a programme of Chopin, Mozart and Beethoven to the Arcaded Courtyard of Wawel Royal Castle. The closing concert is scheduled for 8 p.m. and will feature pianist Zitong Wang, the CORda Cracovia Orchestra and conductor Paweł Kapuła. The event is a current cultural highlight for Kraków because it places a live classical programme inside one of Poland’s most recognisable historic settings. Rather than treating the castle as a passive backdrop, the festival presents its courtyards as part of the experience: music, evening light and Renaissance architecture are designed to work together. A finale shaped around three composers Wang will open the programme with two works by Fryderyk Chopin: the Waltz in E major, Op. posth. No. 44, and the Andante spianato and Grande Polonaise brillante , Op. 22. The evening will then move to Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart’s Overture to The Marriage of Figaro , included in the year marking the 270th anniversary of the composer’s birth. The second half is devoted to Ludwig van Beethoven’s Piano Concerto No. 3 in C minor, Op. 37. The combination gives the finale a clear musical arc, moving from Chopin’s intimate piano writing to Mozart’s theatrical energy and finally to Beethoven’s large-scale concerto form. Wang’s appearance also connects the Kraków festival with Poland’s most prominent piano tradition. The Wawel programme identifies her as the third-prize winner of the 19th International Fryderyk Chopin Piano Competition in Warsaw, held in 2025. Her participation gives the closing concert a direct link to the competition that continues to shape Poland’s international musical profile. A festival built around place Wawel at Dusk has run from 30 July to 9 August this year. Its organisers are Wawel Royal Castle and the Castello Creative Group, with Małgorzata Janicka-Słysz as artistic director and Hubert Piątkowski responsible for organisational management. The 2026 programme has combined chamber music, solo recitals, symphonic works and performances by young pianists. It has also maintained a strong Polish thread, with works by Chopin and Mieczysław Karłowicz placed alongside the wider European repertoire. Karłowicz’s Serenade for Strings was presented on 7 August in a concert marking the 150th anniversary of the composer’s birth. The festival’s two principal venues are the Batory Courtyard and the Arcaded Courtyard. The castle says the Batory Courtyard is not normally open to the general public, making the concerts an opportunity to encounter the historic complex in an unusual evening setting. The Arcaded Courtyard hosts the larger symphonic events, including the 9 August finale. Access beyond the concert hall Wawel Royal Castle describes the festival as an event for Polish and international audiences of different generations. Its format helps make classical music part of the city’s summer public life rather than limiting it to a conventional concert hall. That broad approach was visible earlier in the festival, when a free young pianists’ programme presented Chopin works and jazz improvisations inspired by his music. The main concerts are ticketed, with the castle listing standard tickets at PLN 140 and reduced tickets at PLN 90 for eligible young people, students, pensioners and senior citizens. The finale is an open-air performance, so the organisers advise audiences to prepare for changing evening conditions. The Arcaded Courtyard entrances open at 7 p.m., one hour before the concert. Tickets may remain available at the venue on the day of the performance, depending on capacity. Culture in a historic setting The festival’s appeal lies in the meeting of established repertoire and a highly specific place. Wawel is associated with Poland’s royal and cultural history, while the concert format invites audiences to hear familiar works through the acoustics, lighting and visual rhythm of its courtyards. For Kraków, the closing concert is therefore more than the last item in a summer calendar. It is a compact example of how heritage institutions can use their spaces for contemporary cultural participation while retaining attention to artistic quality and historical context. On Sunday evening, the illuminated castle will provide the setting for the final musical conversation of the 2026 edition: Chopin at the piano, Mozart in the overture and Beethoven in the concerto, brought together by Wang, CORda Cracovia and Kapuła. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: The Jewish memorial at Radegast station, Łódź. Approximately 200,000 Jews from the city were murdered during the second world war. Photograph: piccaya/Getty Images View image in fullscreen The Jewish memorial at Radegast station, Łódź. Approximately 200,000 Jews from the city were murdered during the second world war. Photograph: piccaya/Getty Images Holocaust Letters Enjoy Łódź – but don’t omit its tragic past Dr Richard Bradbury responds to a travel article about the Polish city, home to one of the largest Jewish ghettos during Nazi occupation Fri 11 Sep 2026 13.09 EDT Last modified on Fri 11 Sep 2026 15.37 EDT Share I was shocked to read your travel article detailing the delights of Łódź without a single mention of the city’s past as the site of one of the largest ghettos during the second world war ( A city break in Łódź, Poland’s capital of cinema and factories, 5 September ). The article says: “I ask Anna how Łódź fared in the second world war. ‘It was not too badly damaged,’ she says. ‘Both the Germans and the Russians wanted the industry intact.’” I wonder how the surviving family members of the perhaps 200,000 people who died after being herded into the ghetto, often to work as slaves for the Nazi war effort, would feel about that. Łódź is indeed a wonderful city, and I have watched its transformation since I worked there in the late 1980s. Your article highlights the many great pleasures of the city today, as I too experienced on my most recent visit in July. But as so many have said in the past, if we ignore history, all too often we repeat it. Dr Richard Bradbury Exton, Devon Explore more on these topics Holocaust Second world war Poland Europe Poland holidays letters Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

https://www.politico.eu/article/boris-pi.text: BERLIN — Germany is keen for one of the main missiles used by the U.S.-made Patriot air-defense system to be produced in Europe, Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said Wednesday, as demand for the weapons surges across NATO and in Ukraine. “That is our wish,” Pistorius told reporters outside a meeting of the Bundestag’s defense committee, responding to a question from POLITICO about whether he wanted a PAC-3 production line established in the country. “It is about PAC-3, it is about PAC-2 GEM-T, and theoretically it could also be about Patriot systems, but that is not a decision we can make. We have an offer,” he said. Advertisement Advertisement PAC-3 and PAC-2 GEM-T are interceptor missiles fired by Patriot air-defense batteries to destroy incoming threats. Patriot has become crucial since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, as the system is used to protect cities and critical infrastructure from Russian ballistic missile attacks. The German proposal follows Pistorius’ trip to Washington last week, where he met U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and signed a statement of intent aimed at expanding defense-industrial cooperation between the two countries. Pistorius said Berlin had offered to help meet rising demand for American weapons by bringing more production to Germany and elsewhere in Europe. Boris Pistorius arrives for a meeting in Neuhardenberg, Germany on Aug. 26, 2026. | Pool photo by Michael Kappeler via AFP/Getty Images “The idea is to help meet the enormous demand that has emerged for this and other American systems by setting up production lines in Europe and in Germany,” he said. Any deal would still require U.S. government approval and agreement from the companies involved, including over access to closely guarded American intellectual property. Germany already produces PAC-2 GEM-T interceptors through COMLOG, a joint venture between MBDA Germany and U.S. company Raytheon. The PAC-3 MSE, another key missile for the Patriot system, is currently made by Lockheed Martin in the United States. Advertisement Advertisement That distinction matters because Patriot missiles are in short supply. The U.S. has burned through hundreds in its war against Iran and European governments are trying to replenish their own stocks while continuing to supply Ukraine, creating competition for weapons that manufacturers cannot quickly replace. U.S. troop shifts Pistorius also used Wednesday’s appearance to spell out what Berlin expects from Washington as the Trump administration reviews the future U.S. military presence in Europe. Asked by POLITICO about the Pentagon’s Force Posture Review, Pistorius said Germany expects more detail by the end of this year. “I spoke about it with my colleague Hegseth at the Pentagon, and we assume that we will receive further details toward the end of the year,” he said. The review examines where U.S. troops and military capabilities should be stationed around the world. European governments are watching closely because some forces currently based on the continent could be moved elsewhere, including to the Indo-Pacific. The Trump administration has also been pressing European allies to take on more responsibility for their own defense, raising questions about how quickly Europe could replace U.S. capabilities if Washington reduces its presence. Advertisement Advertisement Pistorius said Germany accepts that some capabilities could be shifted, but warned against withdrawals happening faster than European allies can fill the gaps. “We understand that certain capabilities could be withdrawn in order to use them elsewhere, for example in the Indo-Pacific. But we need a roadmap,” Pistorius said. “The withdrawal of certain American capabilities must not happen in a way that creates dangerous capability gaps, because we cannot procure or fill them in the same timeframe,” he said.

https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-south-kore.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NMy3 'I do not know why the Ukrainian side broke the agreement and made the matter public, but it is very disappointing,' said Lee Jae Myung Image: Anthony Wallace/AFP Advertisement South Korea has demanded an official apology from Ukraine after accusing Kyiv of breaching — and then reportedly denying the existence of — a confidentiality agreement regarding the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to Seoul. Last week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the transfer in an address to the United Nations General Assembly in New York, adding that the soldiers were "not easy to capture alive." Hours later, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung wrote on social media: "I do not know why the Ukrainian side broke the agreement and made the matter public, but it is very disappointing." On Sunday, the South Korean consternation was made official when Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations, demanded "an official explanation and apology." "The presidential office expresses strong regret over Ukraine's unilateral disclosure and its subsequent false announcement that there had not been a non-disclosure agreement," Seong said in a statement. "It is in itself a very serious matter that … seriously undermines trust between the two governments and gravely damages friendly relations between the two countries." Seong said Seoul was "considering additional measures that may be necessary regarding this matter," but did not specify what they might be. Why a new Russia-North Korea road bridge worries Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Ukraine: When were the North Korean soldiers captured? The North Korean soldiers were captured by Ukrainian forces in Russia 's Kursk region in January 2025 — two of around 14,000 North Korean troops deployed to the area to help halt and push back a surprise Ukrainian incursion . Ukrainian intelligence estimates that around 3,000 North Korean troops were killed and another 1,500 injured, with the rest still stationed on Russian territory . To date, no North Korean troops are believed to have operated on Ukrainian territory itself. Ukrainian troops reported that North Korean soldiers who were surrounded or injured on the battlefield preferred to die by suicide than surrender — and only two were captured. Under President Lee, who has attempted to improve relations with the North, South Korea has appeared hesitant to take custody of the pair . But, under Article 3 of the South Korean constitution, North Koreans are still considered citizens of the South and are permitted to live in the South. South Korea is an ally of Ukraine, albeit one which has so far only provided non-lethal aid. But Kyiv has been pressing Seoul to provide advanced air defense systems. Last month, President Zelenskyy claimed that up to 50,000 more North Korean troops could be deployed to Russia. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckgj.text: Image caption, Nvidia chief Jensen Huang reportedly developed a close relationship with Singaporean businesswoman Alice Wang By Julianna Khan Published 5 hours ago China has rejected allegations of a Chinese espionage operation targeting Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, describing the claims as "groundless speculation". US intelligence officials believe that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman linked to Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed, was gathering information for Beijing on the US chip-making giant, according to a report by The New York Times , external . The report said Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was under investigation over the possible diversion of advanced Nvidia AI chips to China and had developed a close relationship with Jensen. Nvidia said their interactions were routine business engagements, while Beijing accused Washington of attempting to smear China. Alice Huang did not respond to the paper's request for comment. The BBC has contacted Megaspeed and the White House for comment. US intelligence agencies had been monitoring Alice Huang and concluded that she was acting on behalf of the Chinese government, according to unnamed sources cited by The New York Times. Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking". It remains unclear what information Alice Huang - who is also known as Huang Le - allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence. At a regular briefing on Friday, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: "The report in question is based on groundless speculation and is nothing more than an attempt to smear China." The paper's report comes amid longstanding US concerns about China's access to advanced computing technology, which is considered crucial to developing artificial intelligence systems. Jensen Huang has argued that allowing Nvidia to sell more of its products to China is important for maintaining US competitiveness in the global AI industry. But Washington has restricted exports of the most advanced Nvidia chips to China since 2022, citing national security concerns and the risk that the technology could strengthen China's military operations. There have however been some loosening of restrictions during Trump's administration. US officials said they had caught several firms illegally trafficking the chips across the Chinese border. They have also investigated whether companies operating through third countries are helping Chinese businesses access the restricted technology. Nvidia has said it complies with applicable export laws and that there is no evidence its chips have been smuggled into China. In response to the allegations made by the Times, John Rizzo, a spokesman for Nvidia, said: "Jensen's interactions with Ms Huang are not unusual or unexpected". He said customers like Megaspeed "receive ordinary business information - not sensitive Nvidia trade secrets - and zero information relevant to national security." He added that allegations the Singaporean company was smuggling chips to China "were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year". Megaspeed told the paper its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation. The company also said it had informed the US government that it was willing to cooperate. It is unclear how closely Alice Huang remains involved with Megaspeed. Photograph: Argentina's security ministry/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Leonardo Bertulazzi, former member of the Red Brigades, being arrested by Argentinian police in Buenos Aires on 29 August 2024. Photograph: Argentina's security ministry/AFP/Getty Images Argentina Ex-member of radical Marxist group scales balcony, escapes house arrest in Argentina Leonardo Bertulazzi, 74, awaiting extradition to Italy, reportedly used harness to flee custody Facundo Iglesia and agencies Wed 11 Nov 2026 14.00 EST Last modified on Wed 11 Nov 2026 15.47 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A 74-year-old former member of Italy ’s radical Marxist group the Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina , the country’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday, after he reportedly hid his ankle monitor inside a tube of pork and lowered himself from a fifth-floor balcony. Authorities placed Leonardo Bertulazzi under house arrest in Buenos Aires in 2024, prior to his extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence. He had received the sentence in 1987 for joining a subversive association and belonging to an armed group. After years on the run, Bertulazzi was first arrested by Argentine authorities in 2002. He was freed a few months later and secured refugee status in 2004, but was arrested again in 2024 after it was revoked. On Wednesday, Argentina’s security ministry offered a $13,000 reward for information leading to Bertulazzi’s recapture after he slipped out of detention. Note from Aldo Moro kidnappers sells for €26,000 at controversial auction Read more The fugitive held a senior position in the Red Brigades, a radical Marxist organization responsible for attacks from 1969 to 1980, dubbed Italy’s “Years of Lead”. The group most notoriously kidnapped and assassinated former prime minister Aldo Moro in 1978. Security footage showed Bertulazzi dropping from a building into a public road as cars drove past. A detective tracking the former member of the Red Brigades reportedly told La Nación that Bertulazzi rappelled down from the fifth floor using a harness. “First, he removed his electronic ankle monitor and placed it in a tube filled with pork, along with a blood pressure monitor to maintain the temperature. He then climbed on to a roof and, using a rope, lowered himself five meters until he jumped onto a vacant lot behind the building where he lived, and then scaled a metal gate to reach the street,” the detective said, according to the publication. The footage, which indicated the time was 6.01am on 10 November, showed a possibly shaken Bertulazzi sitting down to rest for a few moments. Police noticed his ankle monitor had stopped transmitting movement data and headed to the house, where they found the device discarded and Bertulazzi nowhere to be found. Argentina approved his extradition to Italy in July 2025 after the country’s supreme court rejected a final appeal.
